subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and require a launch-readiness fix, or intentionally gate rapid distinct ACPX launches?
rationale: Current code and tests deliberately allow different ACP session keys to run in parallel, so using serialization as the remedy would be a compatibility and product-direction choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
options.body: Run live ACPX/Claude rapid-spawn proof and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

options.title: Gate rapid ACPX launches
options.body: Serialize or throttle rapid distinct ACPX child launches and update tests/docs to make the reduced concurrency contract explicit.

options.title: Defer pending fresh evidence
options.body: Keep this issue open with needs-info until a current live reproduction identifies whether the old symptom still exists.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
recommendation.body: Run live ACPX/Claude rapid-spawn proof and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP spawn/manager source work and ACPX startup work make this the best available owner for the launch-readiness versus concurrency tradeoff.
